title: GorillaDesk vs FieldRoutes (2026): Pest Software Compared
description: GorillaDesk vs FieldRoutes for pest control: $49-$149 per route vs quote-only pricing by active customers, routing, Sentricon/WDO, QuickBooks and trials.
h1: GorillaDesk vs FieldRoutes for pest control companies
body:
GorillaDesk and FieldRoutes both sell software built for pest control routes, but they're sold very differently. GorillaDesk publishes its prices: $49, $99 or $149 a month per route (one route per technician schedule), with unlimited users, a 14-day free trial and no contract. FieldRoutes (a ServiceTitan company) is quote-only. Its pricing page says the monthly subscription is based on your number of active customers, and it offers a demo instead of a free trial. Every fact below comes from each vendor's own pages, checked on 2026-11-20 (GorillaDesk pricing, GorillaDesk pest control page, FieldRoutes pricing, FieldRoutes pest control page). Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown.

{{table:gorilladesk,fieldroutes}}

Pricing: per route vs per active customer

  • GorillaDesk: Basic $49/mo, Pro $99/mo and Growth $149/mo for the first route, paid monthly in USD. Extra routes: Basic +$50/mo for routes 2-3 and +$30/mo from route 4; Pro +$50/mo per route; Growth +$100/mo for route 2, +$50/mo each for routes 3-4, 5 routes for $499/mo, then +$50/mo each. Admin, manager, sales and crew users are free. Only techs who run their own schedule need a route, and crews that ride together share one. The Yearly option gives one month free and is billed for the full year up front. No setup fees, free data migration, and monthly accounts can be frozen in the off-season.
  • FieldRoutes: two packages, Growth ("Ideal for Small Businesses") and Corporate ("Perfect for Scaling"). No prices are published. The pricing FAQ says the monthly subscription is based on the number of active customers, not users or routes. Per-customer rates, setup or onboarding fees and contract length: unknown. FieldRoutes says it doesn't offer a free trial "because of the software's highly customizable nature" and offers a free demo instead.

Worked out from GorillaDesk's published per-route prices (USD per month, before tax, card processing and texting), assuming one route per tech. We can't put FieldRoutes in this table because it doesn't publish any prices. To compare, ask FieldRoutes for a written quote based on your active customer count.

Routing and scheduling

  • GorillaDesk: Basic optimizes up to 25 stops at a time. Pro adds Drive Matrix routing (real-time street routing and drive times) and GPS tech tracking. Growth adds drive time shown on schedules, Best Available Time suggestions and Job Magnet to pull nearby jobs together. Its pest page says you can route all the work for a week or month and assign new work near confirmed jobs.
  • FieldRoutes: Route Optimization is listed in both packages. Its pest page describes batch optimization of "thousands of stops across multiple routes in a single batch", scheduling by proximity and technician specialty, and smart schedules that weigh customer preferences, weather and service due dates. Its routing page says routes can be organized by technician skillset and qualifications, for example termite inspections.

Skill-based routing (sending termite jobs only to licensed techs) is listed by FieldRoutes but not on GorillaDesk's pricing page (unknown for GorillaDesk). See pest control routing software for how these two compare with PestPac, Jobber, Housecall Pro and QuoteIQ.

Termite, WDO and compliance

  • FieldRoutes: Sentricon integration is listed in both packages. The pest page lists WDO (wood-destroying organism) inspection tracking with NPMA-33 access, WDO reporting for California Branch 3, and home diagrams in the mobile app for termite/WDO quotes. Its FAQ also mentions inventory management for pesticides and chemicals.
  • GorillaDesk: material tracking and reporting on Basic ("accurate chemical use records"), plus device tracking and barcoding for traps and devices with trend reporting, multi-dwelling units, and documents and e-signatures on Pro. Its pest page also lists diagramming in the field. Sentricon integration, NPMA-33 and WDO-specific reports aren't mentioned on GorillaDesk's pages (unknown).

Billing, payments and QuickBooks

  • GorillaDesk: Stripe and Square for online and in-field payments (at their rates). Pro adds the customer portal, Stripe/Square subscription billing and QuickBooks Online sync.
  • FieldRoutes: lists FieldRoutes Payments, a customer payment portal, AutoPay, batch payments, automatic outreach to update expired or lost cards, and a QuickBooks Online integration. Card processing rates: unknown (not published).

Texting and customer communication

GorillaDesk texting is a $5/mo SMS subscription plus credit packs: $50 for 1,000 messages, $100 for 2,500 or $200 for 8,000. Credits never expire. Automated email and SMS reminders are included from Basic. FieldRoutes lists automated communication and reminders in both packages. Texting prices aren't published (unknown). FieldRoutes also integrates ServiceTitan's Marketing Pro for direct mail and email campaigns (price not published).

Door-to-door sales

FieldRoutes lists mobile sales capabilities in both packages, and its mobile app page describes door-to-door selling, logging inspections and getting contracts signed from the app. GorillaDesk's Growth plan adds a sales pipeline, sales opportunities, dynamic estimates and estimate packages, and Pro includes sales and production commission tracking.

Which should you pick?

  • Solo operator or small crew that wants a known monthly price: GorillaDesk. You can see the full cost before you sign up and test it on a 14-day free trial with no card. {{aff:gorilladesk|See GorillaDesk pricing}}
  • Termite/WDO-heavy company that needs Sentricon or California Branch 3 reporting: FieldRoutes lists both. GorillaDesk doesn't mention either. {{aff:fieldroutes|See FieldRoutes packages}}
  • Door-to-door sales teams and multi-route batch scheduling: FieldRoutes describes both. Get a quote based on your active customer count and ask about onboarding fees and contract length in writing.
  • Pest plus pool or lawn work: GorillaDesk covers pest, pool and lawn. FieldRoutes covers pest and lawn.

faq: We can't say for sure because FieldRoutes doesn't publish prices. GorillaDesk is $49, $99 or $149 a month for one route (Basic, Pro, Growth), with published prices for extra routes. FieldRoutes says its monthly subscription is based on your number of active customers and only gives quotes after a demo. Checked 2026-11-20.

FieldRoutes doesn't publish prices. Its pricing page lists two packages, Growth and Corporate, and says the monthly subscription is based on the number of active customers. You need a demo to get a quote (checked 2026-11-20).
Does FieldRoutes have a free trial like GorillaDesk?
No. FieldRoutes says it doesn't offer a free trial because of how customizable the software is, and it offers a free demo instead. GorillaDesk has a 14-day free trial with no credit card required.
Do GorillaDesk and FieldRoutes charge per user?
Neither publishes per-user pricing. GorillaDesk charges per route (technician schedule) with unlimited free users. FieldRoutes prices by active customers.
Which one handles termite and WDO inspections?

FieldRoutes lists Sentricon integration, WDO inspection tracking with NPMA-33 access and WDO reporting for California Branch 3. GorillaDesk lists device tracking and barcoding (Pro), material tracking (Basic) and diagramming, but its pages don't mention Sentricon or WDO-specific reports.
Do GorillaDesk and FieldRoutes integrate with QuickBooks?
Both list QuickBooks Online. GorillaDesk includes QuickBooks Online sync on Pro ($99/mo per route) and up. FieldRoutes lists a QuickBooks Online integration but doesn't say which package includes it.
